primitives.name: Wiener-Kolmogorov projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper establishes this correspondence and applies it to prediction problems (projections P_S I, prediction error matrices Δ_S, and Szegő-type infimum quantities δ_S) for q-variate stationary processes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger:
Symbol | Unit | Description
---|---|---
P_S | - | Projection onto past subspace
I | - | Identity operator
Δ_S | - | Prediction error matrix
δ_S | - | Szegö infimum
primitives.assumptions: q-varariate weakly stationary sequence over discrete abelian group G; spectral measure absolutely continuous with matrix weight W integrable and W^{-1} integrable
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when W^{-1} is not integrable, e.g., for deterministic components or non-stationary trends

layer2.mapping: Maps to optimal linear Bayes predictor in GSI using conjugate Gaussian priors; in GSE, yields a derived kernel for multivariate time-series.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive variance from Bayesian regression or mean squared prediction error from conformal calibration

primitives.name: Spectral duality pairing
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Duality: **(F, G)_~** inner products pairing L2(W) and L2(W-1) (Section 2–3).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger:
Symbol | Unit | Description
---|---|---
F, G | - | Functions in L2(W), L2(W^{-1})
G^* | - | Dual group
W | - | Spectral weight matrix
primitives.assumptions: Same as above; W and W^{-1} integrable
primitives.breakdown_regime: Diverges when either W or W^{-1} fails to be integrable

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the predictive information bottleneck in GSI; in GSE, it defines a cross-kernel between input and target spaces.
layer2.telemetry: Mutual information estimates from Gaussian processes or kernel alignment scores

primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper establishes this correspondence and applies it to prediction problems (projections P_S I, prediction error matrices Δ_S, and Szegő-type infimum quantities δ_S) for q-variate stationary processes.

primitives.assumptions: Stationarity, integrability of W and W^{-1}
primitives.breakdown_regime: Vanishes when perfect prediction is possible; diverges for certain non-stationary cases

layer2.mapping: Yields a likelihood-ratio test statistic in GSI; in GSE, it provides a state-transition cost function.
layer2.telemetry: Negative log-likelihood ratios or Kullback-Leibler divergence between predicted and actual distributions

reasoning_traces.think:
The core contribution is a Hilbert-space isomorphism between prediction subspaces and their duals via the spectral weight W. This yields closed-form expressions for the projection P_S and error matrix Δ_S = I - P_S P_S^*, which are fundamental in linear minimum-mean-square-error prediction. The Szegö quantity δ_S emerges as an information-theoretic lower bound on prediction performance. These results are elegant but assume infinite observation length and perfect knowledge of W, which introduces severe bias in finite-sample settings.
